people.role: Mistress of Hàm Nguyệt Trang since 1150: the moon pool, the spirit fish and the pearl beds of Hạo Nguyệt Hồ
people.appearance: A broad, unhurried woman with a diver's shoulders and a pearl in each ear the size of a quail's egg, who laughs before she says no.
people.backstory: Kiều Nguyệt Châu was born in the shore house in 870 with frost in her root, as every child of her grandmother Kiều Băng Liên's (kieu_bang_lien) line has been since the winter of 748, when the old woman sat on the frozen pool and kept the spirit fish alive (C146). The manor has no Ice method to give her, and she has never asked the pines for one. In 942, at seventy-two, she rowed the manor's own boats out from the shore house one by one and sank them, so that Băng Tâm's raiding skiffs would find nothing to take (A013). One of those skiffs was steered by a boy of twenty, Lục Hàn Chu (luc_han_chu). She became mistress when her grandmother died in 1150 and doubled the harvest in twenty years (A015). Everyone on the lake knows how she did half of it: patient beds, better divers. The Lake Hall's tallier Phương Ngọc Sa (phuong_ngoc_sa) has spent forty years on the other half. Kiều drinks with the Lake Warden Thiều Lăng Ba (thieu_lang_ba), sends her grand-niece Kiều Hàn Nguyệt (kieu_han_nguyet) to the pines as the manor's pledge, and pays her tithe a little late every year.
people.wants: To find someone who will teach her grand-niece Ice before the girl's frost goes to waste in the pines, and to keep the manor a manor, not a room of the Lake Hall.
people.secret: Half of the doubled harvest comes from beds off the north shore that Băng Tâm may fish since 944 (C171). Since 1152 Lục Hàn Chu's skiffs have left them alone, and he takes one pearl in ten. That is why the manor's numbers never match the Lake Hall's.

people.backstory: A Backwater Village boy whom Kiều Băng Liên (kieu_bang_lien) took as her last disciple in 1006 because the spirit fish came to his hand. He has kept them ever since and has lit the Moon-Fish Lantern over the pool on every dark night for a hundred and fifty years, since the freeze of 748 taught the manor what the fish need (C146). He thinks Kiều Nguyệt Châu (kieu_nguyet_chau) sells too many pearls and breeds too few fish, and he has said so at every new year for fifty years.

people.backstory: Born in Ngư Đăng Thôn, where the fishers hang lamps on their nets, and named Hàm Sương by a mother who hoped the manor would see frost in her. It saw none. Kiều Nguyệt Châu (kieu_nguyet_chau) took her anyway in 1128 and has meant her to be mistress since she laid a flawless foundation at sixty. The old shore families say a mistress of Hàm Nguyệt should carry the frost, and they look at the Kiều children. She has begun to read Kha Toán Châu's (kha_toan_chau) second ledger and does not yet understand it.

He keeps two ledgers in the shore house: one for the Lake Hall's tallier Phương Ngọc Sa (phuong_ngoc_sa), one for Kiều Nguyệt Châu (kieu_nguyet_chau). Only he and the mistress know what the north beds pay and to whom. He sleeps with the second ledger under his pillow and has never once added it up wrong.

people.role: Mistress of Hàm Nguyệt Trang (820-1150); kept the spirit fish alive through the freeze of 748; sank the boats in 942
people.backstory: In the winter of 748, when Hạo Nguyệt Hồ froze to its bed (C146), she sat on the ice over the pool for three months and fed the spirit fish the moon's reflection with the manor's method. She came back with frost in her root (N-ham_nguyet-02), and every child of her line since has carried it. She was mistress for three hundred and thirty years, ordered the boats sunk in 942 (A013), made the Nacre canon after the war, and died the year her granddaughter Kiều Nguyệt Châu (kieu_nguyet_chau) took the manor (A015).
